title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode. The vehicle did not slow down or stop upon impact. A resident claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing vehicle data, so the stop sign allegation remains unresolved.

This reveals a perception problem in autonomous vehicle deployment rather than an established safety failure. The vehicle's behavior toward the animal did not trigger any intervention system, and it is not established whether the system was designed to detect or avoid small animals or to alert a human operator. The incident prompted Avride to restrict its testing area and to conduct simulation experiments, suggesting the company found the outcome unacceptable even if animal collisions occur regularly in human driving.

What is not established is whether the vehicle's response fell short of its design specifications, whether a human monitor would have changed the outcome, or whether Avride's design choices for this deployment were adequate to the task it undertook.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern. The incident gained attention when a resident posted about the vehicle hitting the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was well-known locally, as it had been nesting in a pot outside an Italian restaurant. Local residents have since preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and acknowledged that while animals are frequently struck by human-driven cars, this event has intensified public skepticism about self-driving technology. In response, the company adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake where the incident occurred. Avride is conducting simulation experiments to improve its technology and prevent similar situations, while ensuring these changes do not compromise overall safety performance. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, continue testing in Austin.
